function.name: range_position
function.description: Where one reading of one LOINC sits against its Anchor v3 published range: below, within or above it, bounds inclusive. pick latest takes the newest reading in the window, pick at the reading at `at`. A sex- or age-specific range is chosen from the subject's stored sex and birth year; facts_used names them, and the age is approximate (birth year only: one of two ages). When a fact is not stored (timing never is) or the age band changes within the reading's year, position is null and depends_on names the facts; nothing is guessed. Reads up to 5000 rows; refuses no rows, mixed units, no published range, and a unit other than the range's (nothing is converted). Neutral position only.

pick.description: latest: the newest reading in the window; at: the reading taken at `at`

at.description: With pick at only: the reading's effective_at as observations_for_subject returns it

function.name: convert_unit
function.description: Convert one value of glucose, creatinine, HbA1c, total/LDL/HDL cholesterol, triglycerides or body temperature between units with a fixed table: value rounded half away from zero, unrounded, unit, the formula used and the rounding rule. Reads no rows. A pair the table does not hold is refused with UNSUPPORTED_CONVERSION and the pairs it does hold.

function.name: cohort_position
function.description: Where a subject's latest value of one LOINC in a time range sits among the latest values, in the same window, of everyone in its synthetic cohort (one value per person, the subject included). percentile is the mid-rank percentile, 100 × (n_lower + n_equal / 2) / n, where n is the people with a value and n_equal counts the subject; say it as "higher than about <percentile> % of the <n> synthetic people with a value", never better, worse or normal. Synthetic cohorts only. Refuses no value for the subject, fewer than 10 people with a value, mixed units across the cohort, and more than 20000 cohort rows (narrow the window).

function.name: conditions_timeline
function.description: List one subject's recorded conditions whose span overlaps the window (onset at or before its end, and no abatement or abatement at or after its start), oldest onset first: code_system, code, display, onset_at, abatement_at, clinical_status and verification_status as recorded (status as of the record, not of the window), with n, n_codes, by_status and n_without_abatement. Optional status and code narrow the list. Reads up to 1000 records; refuses more (ROW_CAP_EXCEEDED) and none (NO_ROWS, with the reason). Lists what is recorded; times relate as before or after, never as a cause.

function.name: cross_source_compare
function.description: How closely two linked wearables agree on one daily measure (hrv, resting_hr, sleep_duration, sleep_efficiency) in a window, over the days both recorded: n_pairs, each source's mean, the mean difference (b minus a), its standard deviation, the limits of agreement (mean difference plus or minus 1.96 standard deviations) and the Pearson correlation. Under 7 paired days the spread, limits and correlation are null. Personal mode only; units must match and are never converted. Says how far apart the two read, never which is right. Refuses SOURCE_NOT_CONNECTED, NO_ROWS, MIXED_UNITS, UNIT_MISMATCH and WINDOW_TOO_SHORT.

function.name: values_around_event
function.description: One subject's readings of one LOINC in the days_before days before and the days_after days from the first recorded onset of a condition (event_kind condition) or the first request of a medication (event_kind medication), found by its code: n, mean, median, min and max on each side and after minus before. Says what was recorded before and after the date, never that the event caused a change. Refuses SUBJECT_SCOPE_VIOLATION, NO_ROWS (no dated record of that code, or no reading on either side), MIXED_UNITS and ROW_CAP_EXCEEDED.

function.name: show_view
function.description: Show a view of one measure in the answer. chart.timeseries draws every reading in window; chart.compare sets window against compare_with (n and mean of each); biomarker.card shows a LOINC's latest reading against its published range, with its trend; table lists the readings (first 50); twin.body shows the body twin on focus with each mapped organ's range position (subject's labs, or none). The server reads the rows itself; the result says how many it read. A LOINC code needs subject (a synthetic subject_ref); a wearable key reads the user's synced data. Never write numbers for a view yourself.

measure.description: A LOINC code, or a wearable key without its date, such as sleep.score; not for twin.body

focus.description: twin.body only: the organ or body system to show
